summary.tagline: The Stubai Valley or Stubaital (German pronunciation: [ˈʃtuːbaɪ̯ˌtaːl] ) is an alpine valley in Tyrol, Austria

days.title: Glaciers and High Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Zuckerhütl
stops.detail: In the rear section, the valley increasingly narrows and finds a striking conclusion with the Zuckerhütl.

stops.name: Stubaier Gletscher
stops.detail: The Stubai Alps quiet area covers a large part of the Stubai Alps (excluding the Stubai Glacier ski area) and extends east of the Ötz Valley to Ranalt in the Stubai Valley.

days.title: Northern Ridges and Mountain Faces
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Serles
stops.detail: The valley is located in the Stubai Alps; significant peaks are the Serles (2717 m), the Habicht (3277 m), the Wilde Freiger (3418 m), the Stubai Wildspitze (3341 m), the Ruderhofspitze (3473 m), and the Zuckerhütl (3507 m), the highest peak of the Stubai Alps.

stops.name: Kalkkögel
stops.detail: The Kalkkögel quiet area is located in the northern part of the Stubai Valley and borders the Stubai Alps quiet area to the southwest.
